requirement_text:
Functional Requirements

2.2.1 Enable agents to broadcast a message to all the agents within the same local network.
2.2.2 Enable agents to multicast a message to all the agents within the same multicast address.
2.2.3 Enable agents to unicast a message to other agents within organization. 
2.2.4 Allow agents to choose among unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
2.2.5 Allow agents to join and leave multicast group.
2.2.6 Provide message encryption and decryption techniques for secured communication.
2.2.7 Allow agents to choose to encrypt or not to encrypt message

Use case Scenarios

Use Case 1: Notify join/leave multicast group
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends notify to join/leave multicast group.
3. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.
For example, Agent_B and Agent_D belong to the same group, and then Agent_B
wants to leave the group and Agent_A wants to join the group. In this situation, when reorganization occurs, Agent_A who is previously not part of the group may send notify message to join the group, and Agent_B who is previously part of the group, may send notify message to leave the group. For instance, Agent_B suffers a failure in one of its
 
capabilities and does not want to receive any further message from the group. Agent_A who may have capability to substitute Agent_B is needed to be part of the group. This involves sending notify of join and leave the group.

Use Case 2: Send/Receive Unicast
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends unicast message to another agent.
3. Another agent receives message.
4. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.
In this situation, Agent_A wants to communicate with Agent_B. This direct communication can happen between any two agents within organization.

Use Case 3: Send/Receive Multicast
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends multicast message to the group (multicast address).
3. Other agents in the group receive message.
4. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted
In this situation, Agent_A wants to send a message to everyone within the group,
assuming that Agent_A, Agent_B and Agent_C subscribe to the same multicast address. This involves the multicast communication since other agents who do not belong to the group cannot receive this message. For instance, an agent may want to inform everyone in the group when the assigned tasks are completed. This is more effective than in unicast communication since only one copy is sent. Also, using bidding/market-based protocols fit well with this kind of communication. An agent may request a bid from other agents
for doing some tasks.

Use Case 4: Send/Receive Broadcast
1. An agent sends message to everyone in the same local network
2. Other agent in the same local network receive message
In this situation, Agent_A wants to send a message to everyone within the same local
network that agent A belongs to. This involves the broadcast communication since any agent in the same local network as Agent_A can receive this message. For instance, when a new agent who does not previously exist in that local network wants to announce the existence to other agents.

plan.objective: Model agent communication selection and execution across unicast, multicast, and broadcast, including multicast join/leave notifications and optional encryption/decryption handling.

decisions.condition: Decrypt multicast join/leave notification if encrypted

decision_strategy: First select the communication mode among unicast, multicast, and broadcast.
If encryption is selected for the communication path, route through encryption before message transmission.
After multicast join/leave notification reception, decrypt only when the message is encrypted.
After unicast reception, decrypt only when the message is encrypted.
After multicast reception, decrypt only when the message is encrypted.
concurrency_strategy: No explicit concurrent fork/join behavior is required by the supplied requirements; message fan-out is represented as communication semantics within the selected mode.
Broadcast and multicast reach multiple recipients conceptually, but the workflow remains single-path from the sender perspective.
exception_strategy: No explicit exception scenarios were provided in the requirements, so no exception handlers are modeled.
Invalid selections are not represented as exceptions; they are excluded by exhaustive decision guards.
termination_strategy: Terminate after completion of the selected communication path and any required decryption.
All valid branches converge to the final node P19, ensuring a single workflow end state.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers most required communication modes and encryption/decryption paths, but it has two semantic coverage problems: the multicast join/leave notification flow is not properly separated by encryption choice, and one branch incorrectly routes the unicast flow into the multicast flow when the message is not encrypted. These issues create required-behavior ambiguity and an incorrect control path.

defects.description: The unicast flow’s 'message not encrypted' branch is incorrectly routed into the multicast flow instead of terminating the unicast scenario after the receive/decrypt handling. This makes the unicast path execute multicast behavior that is not required by the unicast use case.
defects.evidence: Use Case 2 requires: 'An agent sends unicast message to another agent', 'Another agent receives message', and 'Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.' There is no requirement to continue into multicast sending/receiving after unicast handling. The current edge E16 goes from the unicast decryption decision N11 to multicast send N13 on '[message not encrypted]'.
defects.suggested_action: Route the unicast 'message not encrypted' branch to the end of the unicast scenario after receive handling, or to the correct post-unicast continuation, without entering multicast processing.

defects.description: The multicast group join/leave notification flow does not clearly enforce the required conditional decryption behavior for encrypted vs. unencrypted messages before processing the join/leave change. The diagram always sends the notification and then proceeds to a decision, but the join/leave notification scenario requires the message to be encrypted or not encrypted first, and decryption only when encrypted.
defects.evidence: Use Case 1 states: 'Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted', 'An agent sends notify to join/leave multicast group', and 'Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.' The current flow sends the notification at N5 and then uses N6/N7/N8, but the branch structure does not clearly ensure that decryption occurs only on the encrypted path before join/leave processing. In particular, N5 unconditionally precedes N6, and the control flow does not cleanly separate the two allowed cases from the requirements.
defects.suggested_action: Restructure the join/leave notification path so the message is first classified as encrypted or not encrypted, then the notify action occurs, and decryption happens only on the encrypted branch before processing the join/leave change.

strengths: All three communication modes are represented: unicast, multicast, and broadcast.
The diagram includes encryption/decryption handling for unicast and multicast communication.
Broadcast send/receive behavior is present and traceable to the requirements.

unsupported_behaviors: Unicast flow transitioning into multicast send/receive processing on the not-encrypted branch.

changes: Moved the encryption choice for the unicast branch to occur before unicast sending by reusing the existing decision node N3 and its encryption/decryption path.

Removed the incorrect post-receive unicast encryption decision sequence (N11/N12 flow) from the unicast branch and preserved only the required receive step followed by conditional decryption behavior.
Kept all other communication modes, nodes, edges, and requirement traceability unchanged.
repair_history.rationale: The defect was limited to the unicast encryption control flow. The smallest valid repair is to place the encrypt/not-encrypt choice before the unicast send while preserving reception and conditional decryption semantics. To avoid introducing unrelated redesign, the existing encryption decision node and decryption node are reused, and the remaining branches are left intact.

changes: Connected the multicast join/leave notification chain (N5, N6, N7, N8) into the main workflow by adding a control path from the communication-mode decision to N5.

Removed the unreachable/not-well-integrated branch from N3 to N9 and from N4 to N9 by redirecting the encrypt/no-encrypt branches to the multicast join/leave flow and then to the rest of the workflow through existing nodes.
Kept all existing nodes and requirement traces intact, while ensuring the diagram has a single connected workflow and balanced decision paths for PlantUML compilation.

defects.description: The unicast encryption decision is misplaced: the diagram sends the unicast message first, then decides whether to decrypt it, but the requirements state that decryption occurs only if the message is encrypted after reception, while encryption choice is a separate pre-send decision.
defects.evidence: R11 requires sending a unicast message and R12 requires another agent to receive it; R13 requires decryption only if the message is encrypted. The current flow is N9 -> N10 -> N11 -> N12, with N11/N12 handling decryption after send/receive, but the encrypt/not-encrypt choice from R7 is not modeled for the unicast branch.
defects.suggested_action: Place the encrypt/not-encrypt decision on the unicast branch before sending the message, and keep decryption conditional after reception only when the received message is encrypted.

defects.description: The multicast branch is incorrectly redirected into the broadcast flow when the message is not encrypted, causing multicast behavior to be omitted.
defects.evidence: R14 requires sending a multicast message to the group and R15 requires other agents in the group to receive it; R16 allows decryption only if the message is encrypted. In the diagram, E16 routes from the unicast decrypt decision N11 to N13, and N15 then routes the not-encrypted case to N19 and the encrypted case to N16, but N13 is reached from a unicast branch rather than from the multicast selection path, and the non-encrypted multicast path does not clearly preserve the required multicast receive sequence independent of broadcast.
defects.suggested_action: Ensure the multicast branch is entered directly from the communication-mode decision and that both encrypted and unencrypted multicast cases continue through multicast receipt before termination.

defects.description: The join/leave multicast notification flow does not clearly model the required choice between join and leave actions, so one of the required behaviors may be omitted semantically.
defects.evidence: R5 requires agents to join and leave a multicast group, and R9 requires sending a notify message to join or leave. The diagram has a single action 'Send multicast group join/leave notification' and 'Process multicast group join/leave change' without any branch or action distinction for join versus leave.
defects.suggested_action: Add a decision or separate actions so the flow explicitly covers both join and leave notification paths.

defects.description: The broadcast path is not modeled independently from the multicast/unicast encryption logic, which can make the selected broadcast communication depend on unrelated encryption decisions.
defects.evidence: R4 requires agents to choose among unicast, multicast, and broadcast communication. R17 and R18 define a standalone broadcast send/receive flow. Although N17 and N18 exist, the surrounding structure is entangled with other branches and does not clearly isolate broadcast as an independent selected mode.
defects.suggested_action: Keep the broadcast branch directly reachable from the communication-mode decision and independent of the encryption-specific subflows.

defects.description: The multicast join/leave notification flow is semantically inconsistent with the requirement that decryption occurs only when the notification message is encrypted. The diagram routes the encrypted path through decryption, but the not-encrypted path also proceeds through the same multicast join/leave handling structure without a clear termination or bypass that preserves the required exclusive condition semantics.
defects.evidence: R8 states that the message may be encrypted or not encrypted before a multicast group join/leave notification is sent. R9 requires sending a notify message to join or leave a multicast group. R10 states that the message is decrypted only if it is encrypted. In the diagram, N6 branches to N7 on '[message encrypted]' and to N8 on '[message not encrypted]', but both paths ultimately converge on the same join/leave processing flow, which makes the decryption condition insufficiently enforced as a distinct mandatory step only for encrypted messages.
defects.suggested_action: Separate the encrypted and unencrypted paths so that only the encrypted branch executes decryption before join/leave processing, while the unencrypted branch bypasses decryption and proceeds directly to processing.

defects.description: The diagram introduces an additional decision after unicast reception that diverts control from the unicast flow into the multicast/broadcast branch selection, which is not supported by the requirements for unicast communication.
defects.evidence: R11 requires sending a unicast message to another agent, R12 requires another agent to receive the unicast message, and R13 requires decryption only if the unicast message is encrypted. There is no requirement that a received unicast message must branch into multicast decision logic. Yet N10 flows into N11, and from N11 the '[message not encrypted]' branch goes to N13, which is the multicast send action.
defects.suggested_action: Keep the unicast flow confined to receive/decrypt/end handling, and do not route the unicast path into multicast-related actions or decisions.
